title: Dusting and damp wiping: top-down order and controlled moisture
audience: Cleaners who dust and wipe fixtures and surfaces in residential, commercial, bond, short-stay and strata work.
learningOutcomes: Dust vertical surfaces from the top down so that dust does not land on finished work.
Apply a damp wipe by loading the cloth rather than the surface.
Prevent product spray from reaching floors, edges and fittings during damp wiping.
Check and clean the equipment after the task and before storing it.

instruction.heading: Why order matters in dusting
instruction.body: Dust falls. If you clean a low surface first and then a higher one, the dust you knock loose from the higher surface lands on work you have just finished. Working from the top down means each pass deals with what the surfaces above have released, and the lowest surfaces are dealt with last. Use overlapping strokes so that you leave no gaps. Turn or refold the duster when its face is loaded, so that each stroke picks up dust rather than moving it around.

instruction.heading: Dry dusting first
instruction.body: Use a dry duster for the dusting stage, because its purpose is to lift loose dust before any moisture is involved. Dust vertical surfaces such as frames, panels and wall faces from the top down. Draw dust out of corners and along edges with the tip of the duster rather than leaving it in the angle. A dry duster will smear a sticky or greasy film rather than lift it. When you find a film, note it for damp wiping or for a different method, and do not keep working the dry duster over it.

instruction.heading: Damp wiping and where the solution goes
instruction.body: Damp wiping removes soil that dry dusting cannot lift. Make up the cleaning solution exactly as the product label or the business's approved method directs, and do not make it stronger to save time. Apply the solution to the cloth, not directly onto the surface, so that you control where the product goes. Wipe with smooth, even strokes. The working rule is that the cloth takes the product and the surface receives only the cloth. Over-spray can run onto floors, skirting, edges and electrical fittings. It creates a slip hazard on floors and can damage finishes and fittings.

instruction.heading: Keeping the rinse clean
instruction.body: Where a surface needs a rinse, use clean water and a clean cloth, then wipe the surface dry. A loaded rinse cloth spreads soil back onto the surface, so change the water and the cloth when they are visibly dirty. Keep damp-wipe cloths and rinse cloths in their assigned sets, as set out in “Colour-coded cloths: a business-set system that keeps areas apart”, and do not use a cloth from one area on another area's surfaces.

instruction.heading: Protecting the finish and signing the area
instruction.body: Where the business's procedure requires a test on a hidden or less visible part of a surface before a product is used, complete the test first and record the result. Put on the protective gloves and other PPE the job sheet lists before you open a product. Place a warning sign where a wet surface or a fall risk has been created, and keep it in place until the area is dry.

instruction.heading: Checking and storing the equipment
instruction.body: After the task, check the duster, cloths, buckets and trigger sprays for condition and cleanliness before you store them. Rinse and dry reusable items as the procedure requires, and replace any worn cloth. Equipment left dirty or wet becomes the next job's cross-contamination source, so finish this step before you leave the area.

procedure: Place warning signs where needed and put on the PPE the job sheet lists.
Assemble the equipment and check its condition: a dry duster, the assigned cloths, and solution made up to the label.
Dust vertical surfaces from the top down, with overlapping strokes, drawing dust from corners and refolding or changing the duster when it is loaded.
Damp wipe by applying the solution to the assigned cloth, not to the surface, and wiping with smooth strokes.
Where required, rinse the surface with clean water on a clean cloth and wipe it dry.
Check and clean the equipment, then store it ready for the next job.

workedExamples.situation: You are dusting a living room. You dust the skirting boards first, then the bookshelf, then the picture rails.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong with the order, and what should you change?
workedExamples.reasoning: Dust from the picture rails and the bookshelf falls onto the skirting boards you have just cleaned. Start with the highest vertical surfaces, the picture rails, then the bookshelf, and leave the skirting boards until last. Use a clean section of the duster for each high surface.

workedExamples.situation: A glass-fronted cabinet has a sticky film. You spray the glass directly, and the solution runs onto the carpet edge and the timber floor beside the cabinet.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you change for the next cabinet?
workedExamples.reasoning: Apply the solution to the cloth and wipe the glass with the loaded cloth. Protect the floor edge with a barrier or cover if the procedure requires it. Mop up the spill at once, then check the carpet and the floor finish for any damage, and record what you found.

workedExamples.situation: After a damp-wiping session, you leave the buckets and cloths in the hallway, and they are still wet.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should you do before you leave the area?
workedExamples.reasoning: Clean and dry the equipment as the procedure requires, keep it out of the walkway, and store it in its allocated place. Left wet in a hallway, equipment can cause a slip and can spread soil to the next job.

equipmentAndPpe: Dry duster, refolded or replaced when loaded
Cloths assigned to the area, including damp-wipe cloths
Cleaning solution made up to the label or the approved method
Trigger spray used to load the cloth, not to spray the surface
Protective gloves and any other PPE the job sheet lists

commonErrors.error: Dusting low surfaces before high ones.
commonErrors.prevention: Work from the top down, so that dust falls onto surfaces that are still to be cleaned.

commonErrors.error: Spraying the solution straight onto the surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Load the cloth, then wipe. Keep the spray off floors, edges and fittings.

commonErrors.error: Using a stronger solution because the surface looks dirty.
commonErrors.prevention: Make up the solution to the label. Escalate a surface that needs a different method.

commonErrors.error: Leaving wet equipment in a walkway after the task.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean, dry and store the equipment before you leave the area.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Product use follows the label and the safety data sheet. Dilution and PPE are set by those documents and the business procedure.
Wet surfaces and over-spray create a slip risk. Warning signs and wiping up spills are controls set by the procedure. They do not replace checking the route.

qualityStandard: Surfaces are dusted from the top down, with no dust falling onto finished work.
Solution is applied to the cloth and is not sprayed onto the surface, the floor or fittings.
No visible streaks, pooling or over-spray remain after the wipe.
Equipment is clean, dry and stored in its allocated place before the worker leaves.
documentationEvidence: Task checklist showing the surfaces completed and the solution batch used.
Record of any surface that needed a different method, and the reason.
summary: Dust from the top down, so that dust falls onto work still to do.
Dry dust first, then damp wipe with a loaded cloth, not a sprayed surface.
Control over-spray, because a wet floor is a hazard.
Clean and store the equipment before you leave.

knowledgeChecks.question: When dusting a room, which order is correct?
options: Low surfaces first, then high surfaces to keep the room looking tidy
High vertical surfaces first, working down to the low surfaces
Floor first, then all surfaces at the same time to save a few minutes

knowledgeChecks.question: During damp wiping, where should the cleaning solution be applied?
options: Directly onto the surface, so that it is covered fully and left to soak for a while
Onto the floor, so that it runs onto the surface and spreads to the fittings
Onto the cloth, so that the product is controlled and does not reach the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: After the task you find a loaded duster and a wet bucket in the hallway. What is the right action?
options: Clean, dry and store them in the allocated place before leaving
Leave them in the hallway for the next person until the end of the day
Carry them to the next room to finish later and leave them there for now
